Describe a block (areal) support for change-of-support prediction

Source: R/predict.R
block_support.Rd

Defines one or more blocks over which the latent field is to be integrated to a block average – the paddock-scale change-of-support target. Blocks are axis-aligned rectangles (a row of lower / upper bounds per coordinate axis); irregular or polygonal footprints are a planned extension, not supported here. The prediction integrates the GP posterior over each block by deterministic quadrature and propagates the full within-block covariance into the block average's predictive variance.

Usage

block_support(lower, upper, ids = NULL, n_quad = 200L)

Arguments

lower

Numeric matrix or data frame, one row per block, columns aligned to the fit's spatial coordinate axes, holding each block's lower bounds.

upper

As lower, holding the upper bounds.

ids

Optional character block identifiers (default "block1", ...).

n_quad

Integer target number of quadrature points per block (default 200), realised as the nearest tensor grid of axis midpoints.

Value

A gpfield_block_support classed list consumed by gp_predict().

See also

gp_predict()

Examples

blocks <- block_support(
  lower = rbind(c(0, 0), c(4, 4)),
  upper = rbind(c(4, 4), c(8, 8))
)
blocks
#> <gpfield_block_support>
#>   blocks:  2
#>   n_quad:  200 per block
